LESSON: WRITING 4.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are proverbs and sayings important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify proverbs and sayings for information
2. write an imaginative composition using proverbs and sayings
3. appreciate proverbs and sayings for cultural awareness

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 4.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 4.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify proverbs and sayings for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify proverbs and sayings for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify proverbs and sayings for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify proverbs and sayings for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write an imaginative composition using proverbs and sayings

What this means
In this part you learn to write an imaginative composition using proverbs and sayings. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write an imaginative composition using proverbs and sayings.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write an imaginative composition using proverbs and sayings. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate proverbs and sayings for cultural awareness

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate proverbs and sayings for cultural awareness. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate proverbs and sayings for cultural awareness.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate proverbs and sayings for cultural awareness. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify proverbs and sayings for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing to a partner. (skill: write an imaginative composition using proverbs and sayings)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate proverbs and sayings for cultural awareness)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify proverbs and sayings for information.
3. Practise this skill: write an imaginative composition using proverbs and sayings.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate proverbs and sayings for cultural awareness.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are proverbs and sayings important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify proverbs and sayings for information.
5. Be able to: write an imaginative composition using proverbs and sayings.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
